example: In `src/lib.rs`, a method `run` in `impl Thing` has selector `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`; a method `run` in `impl Trait for Thing` has selector `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]`; and a method `read` declared in `trait Read` has selector `trait[Read]/fn[read]`. {cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`
rationale:
Two tests in `src/outline/tests.rs` carry `{test}` references to `requirements.references.selector_impl_and_trait`, and together they cover the example's scenario.

- **`rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` (lines 35–100):** It outlines `src/lib.rs`, the file named in the example. The source has `impl Thing { fn run() {} }`, `impl Trait for Thing { fn run() {} }` and `trait Trait { fn read(&self); ... }`. It asserts that the outline contains `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`, `impl[Thing/Trait]/fn[run]` and `trait[Trait]/fn[read]`. It also asserts that `outline.resolve(selector)` returns a node whose selector equals each one, so the selectors can be looked up as well as generated.
- **`selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` (lines 589–633):** It makes the same assertions for the impl, trait-impl and trait method selectors on a separate source.

The tests name the trait `Trait` rather than `Read`. That is the same selector shape, `trait[<Name>]/fn[<method>]`. The `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]` forms are checked next to each other, so the tests also show that the plain impl and the trait impl get different selectors.

The tests also check an unusual self type, `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]`, which shows the percent-encoding. That goes beyond the example but does not conflict with it.

The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
